label: AQ 0034
title: The optimizer that outgrew the GPU

questions.q: Would SGD with momentum have crashed too?
questions.a: It stores one extra number per weight, not two. Dettmers et al. put 32-bit momentum at 4 bytes per parameter and 32-bit Adam at 8. With ZeRO's mixed-precision accounting that's 12 bytes per parameter, 84 GB for 7 billion (our arithmetic), so on an 80 GB GPU (our example size) it would fail too, though by less.

teach.title: How it works: count the bytes, then cut them

questions.q: Why not keep everything in 2-byte numbers and drop the master copy?
questions.a: ZeRO says the mixed-precision optimizer keeps fp32 copies “to effectively compute and apply the updates”. Our reasoning: an update is usually tiny next to the weight, and fp16 would round much of it away.

questions.q: How would you size memory before launching?
questions.a: Model states: 16 bytes × parameters for mixed-precision Adam. If ZeRO splits the 12 bytes of fp32 master copy and Adam state across N GPUs, each GPU holds 4 + 12 ÷ N bytes per parameter. Then activations, which for a transformer, ZeRO says, grow with layers × hidden size × sequence length × batch size. Compare the sum with one GPU's memory.

teach.title: How it works: count the bytes, then cut them

questions.q: By ZeRO's count, what does mixed-precision Adam store per parameter?
questions.a: 2 bytes of fp16 weights, 2 of fp16 gradients, and 12 for the fp32 master weights, momentum and squared-gradient average: 16 bytes.

teach.title: How it works: count the bytes, then cut them

questions.q: How much model-state memory does a 7B model need under mixed-precision Adam?
questions.a: 16 bytes × 7 billion = 112 GB, before activations. Plain SGD under the same accounting needs 56 GB.

teach.title: How it works: count the bytes, then cut them

questions.q: Why doesn't halving the batch size fix an out-of-memory error caused by switching to Adam?
questions.a: Batch size changes only the activations. Adam's extra state is a fixed amount per weight, the same at any batch size.
